results.title: Korea Times holds first Global Supporters reunion
results.content: The Korea Times held its first Global Supporters Homecoming Day on Friday, bringing together 60 former and current honorary ambassadors of the English-language daily from 35 countries, with the theme “Once a supporter, always family.” The inaugural event brought together members of three recent cohorts. It was a festive reunion for international students and expats in Korea who have served as ambassadors for the newspaper during a six-month term. Participants could network across cohorts and academic backgrounds, taking part in recreational activities with gift offerings. Organizers said the event was meant to keep supporters connected after their terms end, gathering alumni and current members in one place for the first time. “Although we are from different cohorts, it feels special that we are all here together with the same wish to share Korea’s stories with the world,” said Anna Scie

results.title: Kakao founder's acquittal finalized as prosecutors decide not to appeal
results.content: Prosecutors have decided not to appeal an appellate court's acquittal of Kim Beom-su, founder of tech giant Kakao Corp., of stock manipulation charges, making the not-guilty verdict final, Yonhap News Agency learned Friday. Last week, the Seoul High Court acquitted Kim, indicted on charges of violating the Capital Market Act in connection with Kakao's 2023 takeover of K-pop agency SM Entertainment, upholding a lower court's ruling. Friday was the deadline to appeal, but the Seoul Southern District Prosecutors Office said it had decided not to challenge the ruling following a review of both the first-instance and appellate court decisions. The Kakao founder was accused of making large-scale purchases of SM Entertainment shares to push their price above rival Hybe's tender offer price, thereby blocking Hybe's takeover of SM. results.title: 'YOMO JOMO': Seulgi Lee's playful, many-sided look at everyday objects
results.content: What do you see when you look at an everyday object from every angle — or, in Korean, "yomo jomo"? Seulgi Lee, a Paris-based artist who turns Korean proverbs, folk songs and artisans’ techniques into playful sculptures, installations and sound works, poses that question in her first solo show at a public art museum in Korea. “YOMO JOMO Seulgi Lee” opened Thursday at the Seoul Museum of Art's (SeMA) main Seosomun branch and runs through Feb. 28. Lee, born in 1972, has lived in France since 1992 and was selected the 2020 Korea Artist Prize winner. The show brings together more than 70 works, including nine new pieces commissioned by SeMA and serial projects dating to the late 1990s. Lee names her shows around the world in Korean, drawn to the language’s onomatopoeia and mimetic words, which often repeat a syllable in a playful rhythm. results.title: Shin Min-a says she would return for 'The Remarried Empress' Season 2
results.content: Actor Shin Min-a, who played Empress Navier in the Disney+ romantic fantasy hit "The Remarried Empress," said Friday she hopes to return for a second season should it be made. Featuring a star-studded cast that also includes Ju Ji-hoon, Lee Jong-suk and Lee Se-young, the Korean original series follows Empress Navier and her husband, Sovieshu (Ju), whose seemingly peaceful marriage is upended by the arrival of Rashta (Lee Se-young), a former runaway slave. The series, based on a Korean web novel of the same name, which has also been made into a webtoon and racked up billions of views, drew attention as a live-action adaptation of a romantic fantasy story. "It was a long journey that concluded well thanks to the many people who supported the character," Shin told reporters in a group interview. results.title: Parliamentary committee adopts confirmation hearing report for justice minister nominee
results.content: A parliamentary committee on Friday adopted a confirmation hearing report for Justice Minister nominee Lee Yong-cheol, paving the way for his appointment. The report was adopted at a meeting of the legislation and judiciary committee led by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), with the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) leaving the session in protest of the move. The PPP has criticized the nominee over suspicions that he could seek to drop indictments against President Lee Jae Myung. The DPK-dominated National Assembly earlier passed a special counsel bill to launch a probe into allegations that prosecutors under the previous administration had indicted Lee and others on fabricated evidence. The PPP suspects the nominee could order the prosecution to drop the indictments based on the results of the probe. The president faces several trials on various charges, including those

results.title: Prosecutors demand dismissal of Daejang-dong scandal suspects' appeals
results.content: Prosecutors on Friday asked an appellate court to dismiss appeals filed by five key figures in a development corruption scandal linked to President Lee Jae Myung, who were sentenced to prison terms last year. Prosecutors made the request during a hearing at the Seoul High Court, where the five defendants stood trial over their roles in the Daejang-dong development scandal that occurred in Seongnam, just south of Seoul, in 2015, when Lee was the city's mayor. The scandal centers on allegations that a small number of obscure private asset management firms, including Hwacheon Daeyu, were allowed to reap astronomical profits from the project. results.title: Busan seeks path to inclusive city as foreign population grows
results.content: As Busan's international community continues to grow, the southeastern port city is looking beyond attracting foreign residents to a bigger challenge: making sure they can fully participate in everyday life and feel that they belong. Busan Metropolitan City held its 2026 Busan Inclusive City Forum on Friday at Busan City Hotel, bringing together foreign residents, Korean citizens, academics and public officials to discuss ways to build a more inclusive community. The gathering comes as the city's population becomes increasingly diverse. According to figures from the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, Busan had 88,542 foreign residents in 2024, up from 73,185 in 2020 — an increase of about 21 percent. Foreign residents accounted for 2.7 percent of the city's total population in 2024. The figures include not only foreign nationals but also naturalized citizens and children from multicult

results.title: Pioneering educator Trudy Kim, wife of FEBC-Korea chairman, dies at 88
results.content: Trudy Kim, a pioneering educator and the wife of Rev. Billy Kim, chairman of the Far East Broadcasting Company (FEBC)-Korea, died early Friday. She was 88. Born in Michigan in 1938 as the third of four children, she met Billy Kim while studying education at Bob Jones University, where he was an international student from Korea. The couple married in 1958 and moved to Korea the following year, when the country was still recovering from the 1950-53 Korean War. She spent 67 years in Korea, saying she regarded it as her second home. In 1978, Kim founded Central Christian Kindergarten in Suwon and served as its principal for 39 years until retiring in 2017. She laid the foundation for inclusive education, in which children with and without disabilities learn together, at a time when the idea was still unfamiliar in Korea. results.title: Defense minister visits Army's drone testing unit amid push for unmanned systems
results.content: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul on Friday visited an Army mobilization unit operating drone pilot programs, the defense ministry said, as the military pushes to reshape its reserve forces into an unmanned systems-centered force amid a demographic change. Kang paid a visit to the 72nd Infantry Division, a reserve force mobilization unit north of Seoul, earlier in the day, to inspect its drone testing and meet with service members and reserve forces there, the ministry said in a release. The 72nd Infantry Division has been running a drone and robot company under its wing as part of an Army initiative to transform reserve force units into drone-centered ones. results.title: Korea to tighten visa checks on foreign entertainers to curb trafficking
results.content: Korea plans to tighten visa screening and workplace inspections for foreign entertainers to prevent human trafficking, including sexual exploitation and forced labor. The Ministry of Gender Equality and Family convened an interagency policy coordination meeting on human trafficking prevention on Friday, focusing on strengthening protections for foreign nationals entering the country on E-6-2 entertainment visas. The visa allows foreign nationals to work as singers, musicians and other performers at hotels and entertainment establishments. However, some have been subjected to sexual exploitation and forced labor after entering the country under the pretext of pursuing entertainment careers. results.title: Jin Air's Busan relocation complicates workforce integration
results.content: Jin Air’s decision to base its postmerger headquarters in the southern port city of Busan has reignited questions over whether the airline can relocate its key personnel and management functions, with opposition from employees and labor unions threatening to complicate the transition, experts and industry officials said Friday. Starting March 17 next year, the integrated Jin Air is set to officially begin its operations following its merger with Air Seoul and Air Busan. The relocation of integrated Jin Air’s headquarters to Busan came after the local community, which stands to lose Air Busan as a key regional carrier following the merger, repeatedly opposed the plan and strongly pressed for the new airline’s headquarters to be based in the city. results.title: US Apache squadron's inactivation raises questions over combat readiness in Korea
results.content: Analysts are questioning whether U.S. combat capability in South Korea has been diminished after U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) confirmed the inactivation of an Apache helicopter squadron at Camp Humphreys, with no replacement unit yet in place. USFK said Thursday that the move did not affect the allies' military readiness or ability to deter an attack, but the command did not say whether the squadron's helicopters and personnel had been reassigned within South Korea or moved out of the country. Shin Jong-woo, secretary general of the Korea Defense and Security Forum, questioned whether the U.S. could maintain the same capabilities on the peninsula after taking an aviation unit out of service before a replacement was in place. results.title: FIFA, AFC to send officials to Seoul in December for talks on nat'l football chief election
results.content: The global and Asian governing bodies of football will send officials to Seoul next week for discussions on the election of the new Korean football chief, among other issues, sources said Friday. According to the sources, FIFA and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) sent a joint letter to the Korea Football Association (KFA) on Wednesday to inform the Korean federation of the Dec. 4-5 trip. During their visit, FIFA and AFC representatives will meet with their counterparts from the KFA and also members of the government-formed K-Football Innovation Committee, the letter added. It also said the traveling officials would also benefit from meetings with officials from the Korean government and from the Korean Sport & Olympic Committee (KSOC). results.title: Chinese envoy warns US-Korea alliance shouldn't become 'tool' against China
results.content: Chinese Ambassador to Korea Dai Bing said Thursday that the Korea-United States alliance should not become a constraint on bilateral relations between Seoul and Beijing, voicing concerns over Washington's push to modernize the alliance and expand the strategic flexibility of U.S. Forces Korea (USFK). "Any country should maintain its autonomy. We respect the Korea-U.S. alliance, which has a long history," Dai said at a press conference in central Seoul, a week after China hosted the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen. He said China never asked Korea to choose between Washington and Beijing, adding that he believed Seoul has the wisdom to develop relations with both. results.title: [MORNING CALM TALES] Thanksgiving at the USO
results.content: For Americans living overseas, Thanksgiving can sometimes feel like just another day. There are no family gatherings, no holiday parades and certainly no reason to take the day off from work. Life goes on as usual. In Seoul, the subways are crowded, businesses are open and teachers like myself have classes to teach. Unless you make a special effort to celebrate, Thanksgiving can pass almost unnoticed. For much of my early life in Korea, that was precisely how I spent the holiday. I had never been particularly homesick. Perhaps that had something to do with joining the Air Force shortly after high school and spending my first two Thanksgivings overseas in Panama. By the time I arrived in Seoul in December 1990, I was already accustomed to being away from home during the holidays. results.title: DPK lawmaker handed 'severe' disciplinary action over remarks on Lee
results.content: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK)'s ethics committee on Friday decided to suspend Rep. Choi Min-hee, a member of its Supreme Council, from party membership for two years over her controversial remarks about President Lee Jae Myung, sources said. If the punishment is finalized, Choi will be ineligible to run in the 2028 general elections. Choi recently came under fire for her remarks suggesting that Lee, when he was the party's leader, had opposed former President Yoon Suk Yeol's impeachment, and for referring to journalists as "a pack of hyenas." Choi's case was referred to the party's ethics committee after DPK leader Kim Min-seok ordered an internal inspection earlier this month. results.title: Lee's pick to lead capital market reform faces tests on shareholder rights, Kosdaq overhaul
results.content: Meritz Financial Group Vice Chairman Kim Yong-beom, President Lee Jae Myung’s pick to lead a new capital market reform committee, will be tasked with strengthening protections for minority shareholders and overhauling the Kosdaq market, industry officials said Friday. Kim, who reshaped Meritz’s corporate structure and expanded shareholder payouts, will now have to persuade policymakers to act on proposals from private sector experts. The Financial Services Commission (FSC) said its chairman, Lee Eog-weon, met with Kim at Government Complex Seoul on Thursday to discuss the committee’s composition and remit. results.title: 'Who is our main enemy?' South Korea's Gen Z weighs in
results.content: "Who is South Korea's main enemy?" For many young South Koreans, the answer may be North Korea, but being asked the question itself can feel like a test of their political beliefs. In a roundtable discussion organized by the Hankook Ilbo, participants in their 20s revealed nuanced attitudes toward national security, Korean reunification and North Korean defectors. While many identified North Korea as the country's main enemy, some questioned why individuals should be required to publicly affirm that position. Opinions were also divided over the need for reunification, although participants broadly agreed that North Korean defectors deserve support from South Korean society. results.title: Seoul turns to AI to spot falling concrete risks on bridges, overpasses
results.content: Seoul is turning to artificial intelligence (AI) to tackle a potentially deadly hazard on its bridges, developing a new inspection system that can detect concrete at risk of breaking loose without requiring workers to climb beneath structures. The Seoul Facilities Corporation said Thursday it had jointly developed an AI-powered diagnostic device with a private company to identify the risk of concrete spalling, in which pieces of concrete detach and fall from bridge structures. The technology was recently recognized as an outstanding case in the Ministry of the Interior and Safety's collection of successful public sector AI and advanced technology projects. Until now, inspections of bridge decks have largely relied on workers riding elevated inspection vehicles and striking concrete surfaces with hammers, then judging the condition of the structure by listening to the resulting sounds. results.title: Kumho Mitsui Chemicals wins award for sustainability report
results.content: Kumho Mitsui Chemicals has won an award for its sustainability report at the 2026 Korea Sustainability Conference, earning recognition for its efforts to improve transparency in environmental, social and governance disclosures and advance resource recycling in its manufacturing operations. Kumho Petrochemical Group’s chemical manufacturing arm said that its 2026 sustainability report was selected as an outstanding report in the manufacturing category of the Korean Readers’ Choice Awards. Organized by the Korean Standards Association, the awards recognize corporate sustainability reports based on global reporting initiative guidelines and evaluations by stakeholders and experts. The latest report is Kumho Mitsui Chemicals' fourth since it began voluntarily publishing sustainability disclosures in 2023. results.title: Tunisia looks to Seoul's 120 hotline as model for better public services
results.content: A public service hotline built to help Seoul residents navigate everything from transportation to welfare and taxes is attracting attention abroad, with governments looking to Korea’s capital for lessons in making administration more responsive. Seoul’s 120 Dasan Call Foundation said it had conducted 19 international exchanges between 2023 and October 2026, including 17 visits by foreign institutions and two cooperation agreements, sharing its experience with government agencies and public service organizations across several countries. Among its recent visitors were seven senior Tunisian government officials who toured the foundation on Nov. 12 as part of a training program under the Korea International Cooperation Agency’s project to upgrade Tunisia’s national civil petition system. results.title: KOGAS wins prime minister's award for helping small businesses go global
results.content: Korea Gas Corp. (KOGAS) has won a prime minister’s citation for turning its industrial expertise into a broader support network for smaller businesses, helping them develop domestic technology, enter overseas markets and reduce financing costs. The state-run energy company said Friday it received the award at the 2026 Shared Growth Week ceremony held at Coex Magok in Seoul on Thursday, recognizing its efforts to promote cooperation between large corporations and small and midsize enterprises. One of its major achievements was helping localize cryogenic ball bearings designed to operate at temperatures as low as minus 162 degrees Celsius, a technology previously dependent on imports. results.title: Overseas card spending hits record high in Q3
results.content: South Koreans' overseas card spending hit the highest-ever amount in the third quarter of the year on the back of an increase in outbound travelers, data showed Friday. The amount of money spent overseas by South Koreans with credit and debit cards came to $6.63 billion in the July-September period, up 13.3 percent from three months earlier, according to data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The on-quarter rise marks the sharpest since the first quarter of 2023, when the reading spiked 14.8 percent, and also is the largest-ever. The central bank said more South Koreans traveled overseas, although direct purchases from abroad declined. The number of overseas travelers came to 7.12 million in the third quarter of the year, up 7.4 percent from the previous quarter. The combined amount of purchases made through overseas shopping malls, on the other hand, fell 0.8 percent to $1.4 billion.

results.title: Pay-TV subscribers continue to decline; IPTV subscribers slightly up in H1: data
results.content: The number of pay-TV subscribers has declined for the past two years, while the number of people using Internet Protocol TV (IPTV) services has maintained a steady uptrend, data from the country's media watchdog showed Friday. The number of people subscribed to pay-TV services in South Korea fell 0.29 percent from the second half of 2025 to 36 million as of June this year, according to findings by the Korea Media and Communications Commission (KMCC). The number has been dropping since the second half of 2024, the KMCC said. In contrast, IPTV service subscribers inched up 0.47 percent from six months earlier to 21.6 million, accounting for over 60 percent of the market, according to the data. By company, KT accounted for the most with 25.39 percent, followed by SK Broadband with 18.67 percent and LG Uplus with 15.96 percent. results.title: Market volatility expanding amid AI uncertainties: financial authorities
results.content: Global stocks are experiencing increasing volatility due to artificial intelligence (AI)-linked uncertainties, and there is a need to guard against the deepening ties between the chipmaking sector's cycle and the financial market, South Korean authorities said Friday. Earlier in the day, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il held a meeting with heads of the Bank of Korea, the Financial Services Commission (FSC) and other related agencies to check market conditions. The policymakers echoed views that the local stock market's volatility is growing due to uncertainties surrounding the AI sector and changes in the global trade environment. In particular, they said it needs to closely check the risks related to the correlation of the chip sector and the stock market. results.title: Ex-President Yoon's senior aide gets suspended prison term over presidential residence relocation
results.content: A Seoul district court on Friday sentenced a former senior aide to former President Yoon Suk Yeol to a suspended prison term over irregularities in the 2022 relocation of the presidential residence. The Seoul Central District Court handed down a two-year prison sentence, suspended for three years, for former presidential chief of staff Kim Dae-ki after finding him guilty of abusing his power in connection with the case. It also sentenced former presidential secretary for administrative affairs Yoon Jae-soon and former presidential secretary for general affairs Kim Oh-jin to one-year prison terms, both suspended for two years. results.title: Lee Jong-suk proves he's still the romance king in 'The Remarried Empress'
results.content: Despite early criticism surrounding Disney+'s fantasy romance series "The Remarried Empress," Lee Jong-suk emerged as one of its biggest winners, winning over viewers with his romantic chemistry with Shin Min-a and reaffirming his reputation as a master of on-screen romance. The 10-episode series concluded with a happy ending as Empress Navier (Shin Min-a), after divorcing Emperor Sovieshu (Ju Ji-hoon), marries Heinrey (Lee Jong-suk) and embarks on a new chapter in her love life. Based on the popular web novel and webtoon of the same name, "The Remarried Empress" generated considerable anticipation ahead of its release for bringing romance fantasy, a genre widely popular in Korean digital comics and fiction but relatively uncommon in live-action K-dramas, to the screen. results.title: Korea expands customs tech footprint with Guatemala's launch of UNI-PASS system
results.content: Korea is extending its digital customs network into Central America, with Guatemala launching an electronic clearance system developed through a five-year cooperation project designed to speed up trade and strengthen customs enforcement. The Korea Customs Service said Friday that Guatemala officially opened its upgraded electronic customs system, known as UNI-PASS, at the headquarters of its tax authority, the Superintendency of Tax Administration, in Guatemala City on Thursday (local time). The ceremony was attended by Kim Ki-dong, director-general for information and data policy at the Korea Customs Service, Korean Ambassador to Guatemala Kim Deuk-hwan and Guatemalan tax chief Werner Ovalle, along with officials from both countries. results.title: Sungkyunkwan University ranks 24th worldwide in THE Interdisciplinary Science Rankings
results.content: Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) ranked 24th worldwide in the Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027, highlighting its growing strength in interdisciplinary research. SKKU climbed 19 places from last year’s ranking of 43rd to become the top-ranked university in Korea. “This achievement reflects international recognition of our university members’ efforts to tackle societal challenges beyond disciplinary boundaries,” SKKU President Yoo Ji-beom said. “We will continue to advance as a global research-oriented university at the forefront of interdisciplinary research,” he added. A total of 1,058 universities worldwide were ranked in this year’s assessment, released by THE, a U.K.-based higher education ranking organization. results.title: Cadillac launches Korean-designed Vistiq electric SUV in Korea
results.content: Cadillac has launched the Vistiq, an all-electric, three-row large SUV, in Korea. The model's design and engineering were led by GM's research and development arm in the country, the U.S. luxury automaker said Friday. GM Technical Center Korea led the development of the Vistiq, which went on sale first in North America. There, it picked up the nickname "Baby Escalade," after Cadillac's flagship full-size SUV. The Vistiq will be sold in Korea only in the top-end Platinum trim, priced at 181.7 million won after tax benefits for eco-friendly vehicles. The SUV is 5,235 millimeters long and 2,025 millimeters wide, with a 3,094-millimeter wheelbase. It seats six in three rows, with two seats in each row.
